memorial_details:
A square plinth sits on the flat stone base platform, on top with the rectangular tablet which depicts the event and lists the seven casualties. Another tablet is surmounted at the front of the plinth which decorates with emblem of RAF regiment. There are two plaques surmounted at the sides of the plinth which depict the history of the memorial.

The memorial was erected by various businesses and individuals, including David Davies (Business Manager, Space Maker SafeStore Trading Ltd), Susan Ho (Managing Director, Seven Seas Marble & Granite Ltd), Jim Moran (Stonemason, JSM Essex Ltd), Susan Moran (Seven Seas Marble & Granite Ltd), Chris King (Collier & Catchpole Builders Merchants), D.Baxter of DB Concrete, Roy (Loftie) Tolhurst, Carl Jackson (On Signs For You Ltd), Historian Nigel Julian, Michael Heath, Chris Stanfield, N.E.
narrative: On April 25, 1944, at 04:10 AM, RAF Lancaster DV177 of 626 Squadron, based near Wickenby, crashed close to this location, resulting in the loss of all seven crew members. The aircraft, piloted by P/O Murray L McPherson (RCAF), Flight Engineer James D Mayger (RAF), Navigator Francis W Gunn (RCAF), Air Bomber John L Shell (RAF), Wireless Operator Dennis Randle (RAF), Air Gunner Ernest J Fancy (RAF), and another Air Gunner Robert E H Cameron (RCAF), was last seen in the skies above. This memorial stands as a tribute to their sacrifice.

TOP TABLET: THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO THE CREW OF
RAF LANCASTER UM-K2 SERIAL NO. DV 177
OF 626 SQUADRON WICKENBY WHICH CRASHED
CLOSE TO THIS LOCATION 25TH APRIL 1944
AT 0410 HOURS WITH LOSS OF ALL SEVEN CREWMEN.
P
O MURRAY L McPHERSON RCAF PILOT AGE 22
F
S JAMES D MAYGER RAF FLIGHT ENGINEER AGE 21
P
O FRANCIS W GUNN RCAF NAVIGATOR AGE 29
F
S JOHN L SHELL RAF AIR BOMBER AGE 23
SGT DENNIS RANDLE RAF WIRELESS OPERATOR AGE 22
SGT ERNEST J FANCY RAF AIR GUNNER AGE 22
W
O 1 ROBERT E H CAMERON RCAF AIR GUNNER AGE 20

25TH APRIL 2013 BY MICHAEL HEATH,
AND DAVID SEABORN, WITH
PETER POTTER AND SIR BOB RUSSEL M.P.
IN ATTENDANCE. MICHAEL AND DAVID

PETER WAS A MEMBER OF THE SAME SQUADRON

FROM BOTH THE U.K. AND CANADA.
